newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS, PORK BELLIES END MOSTLY LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS, PORK BELLIES END MOSTLY LOWER.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures closed lower but speculative demand and scattered short covering pared losses in the hog pit by the close, traders said.
Pork belly futures remained pressured from a weak cash market and long liquidation in August, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.475 cent per lb lower to 0.150 higher with October off most at 72.525 cents. Pork bellies ended 2.375 to 0.150 cents lower with August off most at 82.525.

Early fund selling, which developed after initial profit taking, subsided when hog futures held chart support near 72.100, basis October. Speculative buying then lifted prices much of the way back by the close, traders said.

Weakness in cash pork prices offset a firmer tone to cash markets to weigh on futures early. Demand for pork has not been as strong as expected and increasing slaughter this week has injected even more pork into the marketing chain, they said.

Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services bought October while Refco sold. Demand was mixed in August. In hog options, RBH bought October 75 calls and locals bought all puts offered across the board following the break in futures, pit sources said.

August pork belly futures remained under pressure from weak cash and finished sharply lower after falling the daily limit on Thursday. Next-year contracts followed after showing initial support with profit taking adding to losses at times, traders said.

Cash 14-16 lb fresh bellies ranged down to $82 per cwt at noon, a $10 setback from last week's high of $92. The break in the fresh market has been much more than anticipated earlier in the week, they said.
However, cash may find support near $80 and this reduced selling pressure late, they added.

Prudential Securities and locals sold February after early buying by R.J. O'Brien. Cargill Investor Services and ADM Investor Services bought August while LFG and LIT division of First Options sold early, pit sources said.
